newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican pension funds sign up 1.185 mln workers.
newsitem.headline: Mexican pension funds sign up 1.185 mln workers.

text.p: Mexico's private pension funds signed up 1.185 million workers as of April 4, according to preliminary statistics obtained Thursday from the National Retirement Savings System Commission (Consar).

A Consar source told Reuters the figures could be revised if workers did not meet the criteria necessary to be registered by the Afores, as the private pension fund firms are known. Official statistics are due next week.
Competition to sign up workers began on February 3, and newspaper columnists say some 80 percent of the first workers to join went to four private pension fund companies.
They were Afore Bancomer, 27 percent, Afore Banamex, 20 percent, Afore Profuturo-GNP, 15 percent, and Afore Santander, 14 percent, the news reports said.
There are 17 Afores competing and the maximum market share they are allowed when all 10 million affiliations are completed is 17 percent.

Columnists have said the pace of affiliation has been slow, with many Mexicans still sceptical about whether their nest eggs are safe with the private firms that will begin operating in July. Also, the Afores have come under fire for the high commissions charged workers who join them.
((-- Cyntia Barrera Diaz, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9549))
